questions.prompt: C is 5×2 and D is 2×7. Which statement is correct?
options: Both CD and DC are defined, with different shapes of 5×7 and 2×2
CD is 2×2 and DC is 7×5, as the inner dimensions are swapped in the product
CD is defined and is 5×7; DC is not defined
CD is not defined, because the dimensions of C and D differ
questions.explanation: Inner dimensions must match: (5×2)(2×7) gives 5×7. For DC the inner sizes are 7 and 5.

questions.prompt: z = A(Bx). Which single matrix maps x to z, and which map acts first?
questions.explanation: z = A(Bx) = (AB)x; the rightmost matrix touches x first.

questions.prompt: For 2D NumPy arrays A and B of compatible shapes, what is A*B versus A@B?
options: A*B is matrix multiplication; A@B is entrywise multiplication
A*B is the dot product of the flattened arrays; A@B is entrywise
Both are matrix multiplication, since NumPy treats arrays as matrices
A*B multiplies entrywise; A@B is matrix multiplication
questions.explanation: Using * where you mean composition is a classic silent bug.
Its first row is twice its second row (determinant 2·3 − 6·1 = 0), so it collapses the direction (3, −1) to zero: 2·3 + 6·(−1) = 0 and 1·3 + 3·(−1) = 0.
Row 2 of A (1, 3) dotted with column 1 of B (4, 1) = 1·4 + 3·1 = 7.

questions.prompt: A is 10x500, B is 500x10 and C is 10x500. Count 2mnp flops per matrix product. How many times more flops does computing A(BC) need than computing (AB)C?
A = [[4, 1], [2, 1]] and Ax = b with b = (5, 3). The second measurement is read 0.02 too high, so x~ solves A x~ = b + 0.02 e_2. Compute ||x~ - x|| (Euclidean norm) to 3 decimals.
questions.explanation: Subtract Ax = b from A x~ = b + 0.02 e_2 to get A(x~ - x) = 0.02 e_2, so x~ - x = 0.02 A^-1 e_2. Here A^-1 = [[0.5, -0.5], [-1, 2]] (det A = 2), so A^-1 e_2 = (-0.5, 2) and x~ - x = (-0.01, 0.04), of norm 0.02·sqrt(0.25 + 4) = 0.0412. It depends only on the 2nd column of A^-1, not on b (check: x = (1, 1), x~ = (0.99, 1.04)).

questions.prompt: U = R(30°) and V = R(60°) are 2D rotation matrices. (a) Compute UV, then (UV)^-1 using orthogonality (no inversion routine), and apply (UV)^-1 to the point (0, 1). (b) A tracker multiplies 100,000 small rotation matrices in floating point and afterwards finds max|A^T A - I| = 4e-12. Explain how this arises, why it matters, and give one repair.
rubric: (b) Each product rounds at about 1e-16 relative, and the errors accumulate over 100,000 products, so the result is only approximately orthogonal: lengths and angles drift (4e-12 is the measured loss of orthogonality).
Repair: re-orthonormalise the matrix, for example with a QR or SVD factorisation, or keep a quaternion and renormalise it; monitor with max|A^T A - I|.
questions.explanation: Open question; check your answer against the rubric. UV = R(30°+60°) = R(90°); because U and V are orthogonal, (UV)^-1 = (UV)^T = V^T U^T = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]], which sends (0, 1) back to (1, 0). In floating point every product adds an error of about 1e-16, so after 100,000 products the matrix has drifted and max|A^T A - I| monitors it.
